shorts.title: Iowa Democrat On Trump: "Better Job On The Border Than Biden" #Shorts
shorts.hook: A Democrat Senate Nominee Says It Out Loud

[beat] [incredulous] Turek said, quote, "He's done a better job on the border than Biden, for sure." Folks, a Democrat said that out loud. On purpose. On a Sunday. [beat] [sarcastic] He also agreed with Trump on no tax on tips, overtime and Social Security. At this rate he'll be endorsing the wall by Halloween. Matthew seven, sixteen: "Ye shall know them by their fruits." And the fruit of Biden's border is a Democrat forced to admit it on national television. [beat] [emphatic] Iowa Democrats, if the border is better now, what exactly are you running against? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe for the daily news roast.

claims.text: Josh Turek, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Iowa, said on ABC's This Week on Oct. 25: "He's done a better job on the border than Biden, for sure."
Turek was answering Jonathan Karl's question about what President Trump has done right, and also said he agrees with Trump that there should be no tax on tips, overtime and Social Security.

shorts.title: Whitmer On Biden's Legacy: "Too Early To Know" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Whitmer Won't Stand By Her Biden Praise
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer was on Meet the Press Sunday. Kristen Welker reminded her of the August 2024 remark that Joe Biden would go down as one of the greatest presidents, and asked if she still believes it. [beat] [amused] Whitmer's answer, quote, "I think it's too early to know what ultimately his reputation and feeling is going to be." Too early! Folks, that's the political version of "I'll get back to you." [beat] [sarcastic] She also said she'd put her money on, quote, "any Democratic governor in the country" against JD Vance or Marco Rubio in 2028. Any governor. Pick a name, Governor. Proverbs twenty-six, twelve: "Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him." [beat] [emphatic] Democrats, name Biden's greatest achievement without Googling it. shorts.title: Judge Halts 500 Miles Of Border Wall, Trump Goes To Supreme Court #Shorts
shorts.hook: One Judge Parks The Border Wall
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Remember the border wall? Federal Judge Kathleen Cardone just parked it. On October second she ordered construction stopped across the roughly five hundred mile Big Bend project area in Texas. [beat] [incredulous] Her reasoning, quote, "The Court finds that Plaintiffs are likely to succeed on the merits of their major questions doctrine claim." Translation, folks: Congress put aside forty-six billion dollars to finish the wall, and one judge hit pause. [beat] [sarcastic] Critics keep telling us a wall is pointless. Funny how much legal firepower it takes to stop one. Now the administration has asked the Supreme Court to lift the halt. Nehemiah four, six: "So built we the wall; for the people had a mind to work." [beat] [emphatic] Should one judge be able to stop a wall Congress paid for? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe for the daily news roast.

claims.text: Judge Kathleen Cardone on Oct. 2 ordered the government to stop construction across the roughly 500-mile Big Bend project area in Texas while the case proceeds, in a preliminary injunction.
Cardone wrote: "The Court finds that Plaintiffs are likely to succeed on the merits of their major questions doctrine claim."

The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court on Oct. 21, 2026 to let it resume building the project; Congress allocated $46 billion last summer to finish the roughly 2,000-mile southwest border wall.

shorts.title: Trump's Iran Choice: "There Will Not Be A Strike" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump Rules Out An Iran Strike, For Now
shorts.narration: [serious] Sunday, President Trump told Fox News the Iran question comes down to this, quote, "Do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off? That's the only question." [beat] [deadpan] Then, leaving for a Michigan rally, he told reporters, quote, "There will not be a strike." Not today, anyway. [beat] [deadpan] That may be the most carefully hedged promise since "the check is in the mail." He also claimed, quote, "we now control the Hormuz Strait." That is his claim, friends. The war began in late February after joint U.S. and Israeli strikes. Ecclesiastes three, eight, in the NIV: "a time for war and a time for peace."
